rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ small force nevertheless swept through every direction, killing or capturing opponents and growing stronger as their enemies weakened, until they entered lands thought unassailable.
rows.anchor: ثم أيدك بأنصار أبرار أخيار فكنتم على قلتكم كالليوث الكواسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enemies could no longer keep the Muslims out and sought a halt to fighting for rest and reconciliation, so the signs of complete victory had become unmistakable.
rows.anchor: وسألوكم في وضع الحرب للدعة والإصلاح

rows.speaker: مجمع بن جارية الأنصاري
rows.claim: At Hudaybiyya, after the Prophet returned to Kura al-Ghamim, he recited 48:1; Umar asked whether it was a conquest, and the Prophet affirmed that it was.
rows.anchor: فلما اجتمع عليه الناس قرأ { إنا فتحنا لك فتحا مبينا }

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The preceding fighting chapter commanded combat and promised divine help for sincere support; this surah answers the believers’ anticipation by announcing the outcome as a clear opening.
rows.anchor: لما أمروا فيها بقتال عدوهم في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The surah unfolds the opening through the fate of oath-breakers and deserting Bedouins, jihad and exemptions, God’s favor on the pledge-takers, spoils, and the promised entry into the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: والتحمت إلى التعريف بحال مننكث من مبايعته صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: He also links the surah to the preceding command not to weaken or call for peace: that command summarizes God’s great gifts, which the surrounding surah expounds.
rows.anchor: فلا تهنوا وتدعوا إلى السلم وأنتم الأعلون والله معكم ولن يتركم أعمالكم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: He reads the warning that God may replace the Arabs as a prediction that Persians and other peoples would enter Islam when the Arabs turned away.
rows.anchor: وإن تتولوا يستبدل قوما غيركم ثم لا يكونوا أمثالكم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s warning about an opening in the barrier of Gog and Magog is cited alongside the replacement verses as a sign of the Arabs’ coming loss of dominance to other peoples.
rows.anchor: فتح اليوم من ردم يأجوج ومأجوج مثل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī identifies the barrier’s neighboring peoples with the Persians and their regions, and says their later control of religious, administrative, and scholarly offices under al-Manṣūr was an opening that exalted Islam.
rows.anchor: وكان فتحا وعزا وظهورا لكلمة الإسلام

rows.speaker: عمر وحذيفة
rows.claim: In the fitna report, Umar asks whether the closed door between him and tribulation would be opened or broken; Hudhayfa says broken, which signifies Umar’s killing and distinguishes breaking from opening.
rows.anchor: إن بينك وبينها بابا مغلقا

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī ranks Khorasan’s scholars strongest in reasoning, describing them as Persian by ancestry and homeland but Arab in creed, and as fulfilling the Prophet’s promise when Arabs abandoned learning for worldly life.
rows.anchor: وأمضاهم في النظر عزيمة وأقواهم فيه شكيمة أهل خراسان

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the Companions asked who would replace them, the Prophet pointed to Salman and said that men from his people would attain faith even if it were at the Pleiades.
rows.anchor: لو كان الإيمان في الثريا لناله رجال من هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening after the chapter of those who disbelieved promises the believers’ rise and the unbelievers’ retreat, in a sequence that also links the victory and the Sūrat al-Naṣr to al-Kāfirūn.
rows.anchor: بشارة بظهور أهل هذا الدين وإدبار الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reads the forgiveness attached to the opening as an allusion to the Prophet’s death: his worldly mission culminates in manifesting the true religion and erasing falsehood.
rows.anchor: علل الفتح بالمغفرة وما بعدها رمزا إلى وفاة النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is one of three signs of the Prophet’s approaching death and the chief sign that his religion would prevail over every rival.
rows.anchor: فالفتح الذي هو أحد العلامات الثلاث المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from the majestic first-person plural to the third-person name Allah signals supreme majesty and makes the forgiveness accord with the comprehensive divine name embracing all beautiful names.
rows.anchor: بالانتقال من أسلوب العظمة بالنون إلى أسلوب الغيبة المشير إلى غاية الكبرياء بالإسناد إلى الاسم الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier ‘sin’ is the matter for which the Prophet had been told in the fighting surah to seek forgiveness; it denotes moving from a complete station to a still higher one, so the former appears deficient by comparison.
rows.anchor: أي الذي تقدم في القتال أمرك بالاستغفار له

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī explains that forgiveness has degrees just as sins do, invoking the maxim that the good deeds of the righteous count as misdeeds for those brought near.
rows.anchor: المغفرة المعتبرة لها درجات كما أن الذنوب لها درجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, forgiveness means the Prophet will witness it after moving from knowledge of certainty to seeing certainty and true certainty.
rows.anchor: لتشاهد المغفرة باللنقلة إلينا بعد علم اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reads the Prophet’s death after victory as the completion of his mission: the Arabs enter Islam, his followers guide humanity, and Satan despairs of open worship in the peninsula.
rows.anchor: أن الله يتوفاه صلى الله عليه وسلم عقب الفتح ودخول جميع العرب الذين يفتتحون جميع البلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The completion of favor has two parts: the religion’s public triumph and the Prophet’s transfer from the visible, transient world to the unseen, enduring realm among the prophets.
rows.anchor: إظهار الدين والتقلة إلى مرافقة النبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance promised to the Prophet is the guidance of his whole community, a clear and exalted straight path through an unerring Book that requires steadfast adherence.
rows.anchor: أي واضحا جليلا جليا موصلا إلى المراد من كتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mighty victory comes through the community’s triumph over the nations and removal of affliction; it is enduring, leaves the community unconquered, and cannot be annulled.
rows.anchor: أي يغلب المنصور به كل من ناواه ولا يغلبه شيء مع دوامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Sūrat Qāf closes with a warning, this surah opens with a solemn oath to establish that the promised outcome is true, matching the oath to its subject.
rows.anchor: افتتح هذه بالقسم البالغ على صدقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘scatterers’ are winds that disperse and drive things away; the wording ‘scattering’ stresses their function under angelic direction.
rows.anchor: أي الرياح التي من شأنها الإطارة والرمي والتفريق والإذهاب

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Aṣbahānī describes winds as moving beneath the wings of the Throne-bearing cherubim, then through successive regions and cardinal paths with fixed boundaries.
rows.anchor: الرياح تحت أجنحة الكروبيين حملة العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘heavy-bearing’ are clouds formed when winds disperse vapor, lift it, gather it, and carry water, lightning, and whatever else God places in them; their unseen load shows divine power.
rows.anchor: أي من السحب التي فرقت الريح أصلها وهو الأبخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘runners easily’ are clouds traveling freely across the sky, and also ships moving easily across the sea despite the weight of their cargo.
rows.anchor: وكذا جري السفن في باحة البحر بعد ثقلها بالوسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath presents a causal sequence: wind disperses vapor, clouds carry it, and their travel culminates in water being divided among distant lands as mercy or punishment.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك التفريق هو غاية الجري المترتب على الحمل المترتب على الذرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘distributors of a matter’ include clouds directed by angels, ships moved by gentle or violent winds, and everything angels allocate among people by God’s command.
rows.anchor: أي من السحب بما تصرفها فيه الملائكة عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apportioned matters include both mercy and punishment.
rows.anchor: أي من الرحمة أو العذاب

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says God swears by created wonders to strengthen belief and prompt reflection, whereas people swear by God as witness to a claim known to Him in secret and public.
rows.anchor: هذه أقسام يقسم الله بها ولا يقسم بها الخلق لأن قسم الخلق استشهاد على صحة قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Measured winds, suspended water-laden clouds, regulated ship movement, and angelic distribution all testify to a wise, powerful Creator; excess, cessation, or stillness can destroy.
rows.anchor: ولو انقطعت بتسخير البحر لجريانها وتقدير الريح لها بما لو زاد لغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything promised, reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience, is truthful even if its causes remain unseen; its realization will prove the report true.
rows.anchor: أي من الوعد للطائع والوعيد للعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the promised event ‘truthful’ as an active participle makes its certainty and nearness seem present; when it arrives, its truth will be plain.
rows.anchor: أي مطابق الإخبار به للواقع

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barjān says every divine oath matches significant qualities in the object sworn by and guides whom God wills, though sensory appearances and distractions obscure its signs.
rows.anchor: ما أقسم بقسم إلا مطابقا معناه لمعان في المقسم من أجله بسراج منير يهدي به الله تعالى

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī takes God’s power over extraordinary phenomena that defy ordinary nature as evidence of His power to resurrect.
rows.anchor: استدل باقتداره على هذه الأشياء العجيبة المخالفة لمقتضى الطبيعة على اقتداره على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The dīn’ means both each person’s recompense at resurrection and the revealed religion; it will certainly occur, Islam will prevail over other religions, and everyone will be gathered for judgment.
rows.anchor: أي المجازاة لكل أحد بما كسب يوم البعث

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the oath and the assertion of judgment to Sūrat Qāf’s account of death and the afterlife, then cites warnings that God does not overlook wrongdoers and prolongs their respite to increase their sin.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه المواعيد الأخروية في سورة ق وعظيم تلك الأحوال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: After affirming the promise and recompense, the surah exposes the disbelievers’ denial and scorn as they ask when Judgment Day will be.
rows.anchor: عقب ذلك بتكذيبهم بالجزاء وازدرائهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The description of the two groups and their different ends leads to signs on earth for the certain, rebuking those who do not reflect on creation’s wonders.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى حال الفريقين وانتهاء الطريقين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Earlier peoples repeatedly accused their messengers of sorcery or madness, showing that the present deniers repeat an established pattern.
rows.anchor: كذلك ما أتى الذين من قبلهم من رسول إلا قالوا ساحر أو مجنون

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The question whether deniers taught one another their stance or are simply transgressive points to arrogance and darkened hearts as the common cause of their disbelief; God could have guided every soul.
rows.anchor: أي عجبا لهم يف جريهم على التكذيب والفساد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to turn away from them without blame.
rows.anchor: فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The Prophet’s reward lies in reminding and calling people to God; the reminder benefits believers, and those destined for felicity respond to it.
rows.anchor: وذكر فإن الكذرى تنفع المؤمنين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The wrongdoers will receive a share of punishment like that suffered by their predecessors who followed the same path.
rows.anchor: وإن للذين ظلموا ذنوبا مثل ذنوب أصحابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky’s ‘paths’ are intricately woven courses of stars, beautifully and firmly arranged, combining separation and connection, agreement and difference; al-Rāzī says the root denotes firm extension and regularity.
rows.anchor: أي الآيات المحتبكة بطرائق النجوم المحكمة

rows.speaker: قريش
rows.claim: Quraysh call the revelation poetry, a charge Biqāʿī says should entail the regular meter, unified rhyme, sweetness, and grace of actual poetry.
rows.anchor: هذا شعر فيلزمكم وصفه بما تصفون به الشعر

rows.speaker: قريش
rows.claim: Quraysh call the revelation magic, but Biqāʿī argues that this would mean it has no realities despite its meanings being firmer than mountains.
rows.anchor: هذا سحر فيلزمكم مع الإفرار بالعجز عنه

rows.speaker: قريش
rows.claim: Quraysh call it confused dreams, which would require it to lack stable meaning and be easy for anyone to fabricate.
rows.anchor: فيلزمكم أنه لا ينضبط بضابط

rows.speaker: قريش
rows.claim: Quraysh call it soothsaying, which would entail accepting its disclosures of unseen events, hidden matters, and decisive judgments.
rows.anchor: إنه كهانة فيلزمكم أن تعتقدوا منه ما تعتقدون

rows.speaker: قريش
rows.claim: They also call the Prophet a madman and a liar, while simultaneously claiming to be rational and the most truthful people.
rows.anchor: إنه شاعر وساحر ومجنون وكاهن وكاذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contradictory accusations, and their mismatch with Quraysh’s own claims to reason and honesty, reveal their confused conduct and a force that overpowers them; they are signs in the world and within themselves.
rows.anchor: فهما آيتان في الآفاق وفي أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah condemns desire because attachment to the transient world produces misguidance and blindness, while it praises knowledge for guiding people toward the enduring afterlife and its happiness or misery.
rows.anchor: ذم الهوى لإنتاجه الضلال والعمى بالإخلاد إلى الدنيا التي هي دار الكدور والبلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah urges following the Prophet’s warnings and glad tidings: he does not speak from whim, because his knowledge and exposition come from God; resurrection and gathering manifest divine wisdom by raising the purified and humiliating the wicked.
rows.anchor: لأن علمه هنو العلم لأنه لا ينطق عن الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Najm is explained through reflection on the oath, its answer, and the way the Book is arranged in star-like patterns.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك دل اسمها النجم عن تأمل القسم والجواب وما نظم به من نجوم الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, God’s encompassing perfection entails that His messenger is of perfection; al-Raḥmān’s mercy reaches all created beings, while al-Raḥīm’s favor specifically rescues His devotees from error and guides them to pleasing conduct.
rows.anchor: خص أهل وده بالإنقاذ من الضلال والهداية إلى ما يرضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Have you considered’ means ‘tell Me’ with informed inward and outward perception, prompted by the signs proving the Prophet’s message; the named deities were major idols of their peoples.
rows.anchor: أي أخبروني بسبب ما تلوت عليكم من هذه الآيات الباهرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Lāt was an idol of Thaqīf, al-ʿUzzā a tree of Ghatafān, and Manāt a stone of Hudhayl and Khuzāʿa; the first two were objects of oath-taking.
rows.anchor: { اللات } وهو صنم ثقيف { والعزى } وهي شجرة لغطفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Manāt the third and ‘other’ reflects its lower rank in their scheme and exposes the irrationality of adding a third deity, even one they considered inferior and feminine.
rows.anchor: أي إنه ما كفاهم في خرق سياج منها العقل في مجرد تعديد الإله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their feminine names reflect their belief that goddesses resembled angels, whom they falsely claimed were God’s daughters; the inferior female type is assigned to God while they claim the superior male type for themselves.
rows.anchor: وأنثوا أسماءها تشبيها لها بالملائكة على زعمهم بأنها بنات الله

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the idol names were made feminine by analogy with angels, who were falsely regarded as God’s daughters.
rows.anchor: وأنثوا أسماءها تشبيها لها بالملائكة على زعمهم بأنها بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī rejects the gharānīq story as a feeble report and nonsense in this context: the denunciatory question and the phrase ‘those lofty beauties’ cannot be connected in the passage’s eloquent argument.
rows.anchor: بطلان ما نقل نقلا واهيا من أنه قيل حين قرئت هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols neither revealed scripture, sent messengers, performed signs, nor could harm or benefit; claiming they were God’s daughters adds the defect of assigning Him the inferior sex despite His freedom from need or likeness.
rows.anchor: لم تنزل لكم وحيا ولا أرسلت لكم رسولا ولا فعلت مع أحد منكم شيئا مما كرمنا به عبدنا محمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question condemns the asymmetry: men claim the superior male type for themselves and assign the inferior female type exclusively to God.
rows.anchor: أي خاصة { الذكر } أي النوع الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their allocation is unjust, deficient, and crooked, especially because they despised daughters so deeply that they buried them alive yet attributed daughters to God.
rows.anchor: أي جائرة ناقصة ظالمة فيما يحسن للحق للغاية عرجاء غير معتدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses ellipsis by cross-omission: naming the goddesses in the rebuke implies denial that they are deities, while attributing females to God implies that the Arabs reserve males for themselves.
rows.anchor: دل ذكر اسمها في أسلوب الإنكار على حذف إنكار كونها آلهة
